correctness.rationale: For every admissible positive part-size vector, the multiplicity of a fixed quotient spanning tree is the product of the part-size falling factorials. Contraction of a projected matching and the weighted Cayley identity give a closed forest-restricted Prüfer polynomial. The factorial transform equals the product of the pair weights times an exact binomial factor; normalization by the known total count yields the claimed joint inclusion law. Covariance is an exact subtraction, with k>=4 and M>=2 for disjoint edges. Exact finite tests include 6312 quotient-tree tests and 6 independent physical enumerations; they corroborate but do not substitute for the full proof.

value.rationale: The initiating paper motivates random feasible interconnection design in multipartite systems. Exact simultaneous part-pair link probabilities and conditional inclusion are natural probabilistic observables, and their all-orders falling-factorial form gives structural information rather than routine total counting. Strict positive covariance for disjoint quotient links contrasts with classical independence for disjoint edges in uniform Cayley trees; it is a meaningful qualitative boundary caused by physical vertex capacities. Scope extends over infinitely many admissible part sizes and matching sizes.
